stories.title: Sleeper Vande Bharat Express to run between Varanasi and Chheharta:PM Modi to flag off train on July 17, service to operate thrice a week
stories.summary: The country's second sleeper Vande Bharat Express train will run between Varanasi and Chheharta in Amritsar. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will flag it off from Jalandhar on July 17. This train will be named Sant Ravidas Express. The train's schedule has been released by the Railways. The Prime Minister will flag it off from Jalandhar via video conferencing. On the same day, the PM will inaugurate Jalandhar's new railway station. Operation will be three days a week According to the letter issued by the Railway Board, the Vande Bharat sleeper train running from Chheharta to Varanasi will be named Sant Ravidas Express. Its train number has been kept as 14624/14623. It will operate only three days a week. Train number 14624 from Chheharta will run every Wednesday, Friday, and Sunday at 2:05 PM. Train number 14623 from Varanasi will run every Thursday, Saturday, and Monday at 7:05 PM. And will reach Chheharta at 5:10 PM the next day. Train Schedule Stoppages at these stations The Vande Bharat Sleeper Express train will have stoppages between Varanasi and Chheharta at Jaunpur City, Sultanpur, Lucknow, Shahjahanpur, Bareilly, Moradabad, Saharanpur, Ambala Cantt, Ludhiana, Jalandhar City, and Amritsar. The primary maintenance of the train will be at Chheharta station.

stories.title: Cheating gang targeting Boring Technician exam arrested:UP STF nabs candidate from Varanasi and solver from Prayagraj; FIR filed against 13
stories.summary: A case of cheating using electronic devices has come to light during the Assistant Boring Technician examination of the Minor Irrigation Department in Varanasi. Two candidates were caught cheating in the examination conducted by the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission. In the same case, the UP STF has arrested the gang leader helping candidates cheat and 11 other people from Prayagraj. The candidates paid ₹5 lakh each to Captain Singh Patel, the mastermind of the cheating gang. Currently, cases have been registered against the 13 accused caught from Varanasi and Prayagraj at Kotwali and Sigra police stations. The examination was under STF surveillance when officials received inputs about cheating. STF Inspector Anil Kumar Singh informed that the field unit Varanasi was active during the examination. During this time, officials received information that a gang involved in cheating in competitive examinations using micro-electronic devices after collecting large sums of money. Following this, the team coordinated with the Prayagraj unit and started the investigation. During this, officials learned that Shivjeet Patel, the ringleader of the gang facilitating cheating through micro-electronic devices, and his brother Captain Singh Patel were present with solvers in a room in Kothari village, Bahariya police station, Prayagraj. Solvers were answering questions for two candidates through electronic devices. Acting on this information, the STF Varanasi team raided the location and arrested the gang leader and solvers from there. Two candidates arrested from Harishchandra Balika and Anglo Muslim School Anil Kumar Singh stated that an STF team, based on the tip-off, arrested one candidate from each examination centre carrying an electronic device from Harishchandra Balika Inter College located in Maidagin and Anglo Muslim School in Lallapura area. Gang charged ₹5 lakh from each candidate The accused revealed during interrogation that Captain Singh Patel, his brother Shivjeet Patel, Deepak Patel, and Rajendra Yadav alias Dhirendra Yadav have an organized gang for cheating in competitive exams. The racket was masterminded by Shivjeet Patel. They all contact certain candidates appearing in various competitive exams through their relatives and acquaintances, gaining their trust that they will clear the examination with the help of a solver. In return, ₹5 lakh was charged. Those arrested include:

stories.title: Free treatment up to ₹5 lakh, ₹1.60 crore accident cover:UP teachers and non-teaching staff can apply; these documents are mandatory
stories.summary: Government teachers in UP will get accidental insurance of ₹1 crore 60 lakh and cashless treatment up to ₹5 lakh. The insurance will provide financial security in case of a major accident. Cashless treatment will cover hospital expenses during serious illness. Shikshamitras, instructors, and cooks will also be covered under this scheme. Approximately 12 lakh teachers and non-teaching staff of the Basic and Secondary Education Department will benefit from this. This facility will be provided under the "Chief Minister Teacher Cashless Medical Scheme". All Education Department Staff to Get Accidental Insurance This facility will be available under SBI's Corporate Salary Package (CSP). If a teacher dies in a road, rail, or air accident, their nominee will receive an insurance amount of up to ₹1.60 crore. If a teacher becomes completely disabled in an accident, they will receive insurance benefits according to the prescribed rules. Normal death due to illness or heart attack is not covered under this insurance. Cashless treatment up to ₹5 lakh will also be free This facility will be available under the Chief Minister Teacher Cashless Medical Scheme, which will be operated by SACHIS. It is a government agency, whose full name is State Agency for Comprehensive Health and Integrated Services. If a teacher or their dependent family member falls ill and is admitted to a hospital, cashless treatment up to ₹5 lakh per year can be availed in UP's government hospitals, medical colleges, and private hospitals associated with SACHIS. This facility will be available again every year. Create a Cashless Medical Card in 10 Simple Steps Register by September 6 Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had announced the Chief Minister Teacher Cashless Medical Scheme last year on Teacher's Day (September 5). The Chief Minister formally launched the scheme on July 8, 2026. All eligible teachers and non-teaching staff must complete their and their family's registration by September 6, 2026, so that the verification process can be completed. According to Archana Verma, CEO of SACHIS, a portal has been created for the registration, verification, and issuance of health cards for teachers. More than 7.89 lakh beneficiaries from the Basic Education Department have already registered their data. The portal for the Secondary Education Department has also been launched. Soon, teachers from the Higher Education Department will also join this scheme. After verification and e-KYC, teachers will be able to download their health cards and avail the benefits of cashless treatment. Not a single rupee to be paid from pocket According to the government order, the annual premium for a teacher under this scheme will be around ?3,000. The entire payment will be made by the government from its departmental budget. Employees will not have to pay a single rupee of premium from their own pockets. This scheme will be applicable only after the patient is admitted to the hospital. It will benefit in the treatment of more than 1900 diseases including cancer, heart disease, kidney disease, neuro, and surgery. OPD expenses for common cold or just consulting a doctor and taking medicine are not included in this. Answers to 4 important questions for teachers and staff Question 1- What do I need to do to avail the benefits of cashless treatment and insurance scheme? Answer- To avail cashless treatment, you will need to register on the portal of the Education Department and 'SACHIS'. After this, the department will issue you a 'Cashless Health Card'. Your salary account must be with SBI. Question 2- If an unfortunate incident happens to an employee within the hospital, how will the money for children's education and marriage be received? Answer- If an accident happens to an employee, the family will not only receive insurance money. Separate financial assistance will also be provided for children's education and daughters' marriages. Necessary documents will have to be submitted for this. After the investigation is complete, this amount will be sent directly to the bank account. Question 3- Will this facility also be valid in hospitals outside UP? Answer- This facility will only be available in UP government hospitals and private hospitals associated with 'Sachis'. No money will be taken from the patient. More than 1900 treatment packages are already fixed. Therefore, the government will directly pay the hospital. Question 4- What are the conditions for the ?2 lakh cover being provided to cooks and contract workers? Answer- Cooks and other contract employees earning less than ?10 thousand will have a zero-balance account opened in SBI. Upon activation of the debit card, an accidental insurance of ?2 lakh will be provided. No separate paperwork will be required for this.

stories.title: Married lovers die by suicide in Kanpur hotel:Man records reel before death; woman tells husband she consumed poison
stories.summary: In a hotel in Kanpur, a couple died by suicide by consuming poison. The woman was from Unnao and the man was from Fatehpur. Both were married and had left their respective homes with a plan to die. The incident came to light on Saturday evening at 4 PM, when a screaming sound came from the hotel room. When the hotel staff opened the door with another key, the young man was lying unconscious on the bed, while the woman was lying nearby and screaming for water. Both were taken to Ursala Hospital, where doctors declared both of them dead. On Sunday, police investigation revealed that before reaching the hotel, the young man had made a reel on Instagram. In which he had said, “If I write a book of my pain, people will be afraid of love...”. He also wrote, "I am going to die". Meanwhile, the woman called her husband and said, “I have consumed poison, now live happily with the children...” and then cut the call. About a month ago, both of them left their families and fled to Gujarat, from where the police recovered them and handed them over to their relatives. Despite the strictness of the family and the police, both came into contact again and decided to die together when the path to living together was closed. Based on call details, social media posts, and chats, the police are investigating the entire matter, considering it a pre-planned suicide. The post-mortem of both bodies was conducted on Sunday evening around 4 PM. Shivangi ran away with her lover on June 9 On Saturday, police found two bodies at Hotel Surya located at Ghantaghar in Kanpur. They were identified as Shivangi (33) from Unnao and Digvijay (35), a young man from Fatehpur. Dheeru Tiwari, a resident of Magarwara, Unnao, works in the travel business in Gujarat. At home, he has his wife Shivangi, a seven-year-old daughter, and a nine-year-old son. Dheeru stated that his life was going very well, but a year ago, his wife Shivangi became friends with Digvijay, a resident of Radha Nagar, Fatehpur, through Facebook. Dheeru said, "I lived in Gujarat. Shivangi and Digvijay took advantage of this, and their closeness grew. When the family became aware of the matter, I also protested. When the discord increased over this issue, on June 9, 2026, Shivangi left me and the children and ran away from home with her lover Digvijay." According to the police, Shivangi's husband Dheeru Tiwari and brother Himanshu Shukla registered a missing person report for Shivangi at the police station. The police recovered both of them from Gujarat. Both were released on the condition that they would no longer have any relationship with each other. Even both their SIM cards were broken at the police station. After this, both started using new mobile numbers, but within a month, they started talking again. Both decided to die together due to restrictions. After spending three hours together in the hotel room, they committed suicide on Saturday afternoon. Shivangi called her husband and said - now live happily ACP Collectorganj Anand Kumar Ojha said, “Digvijay, a resident of Radha Nagar, Fatehpur, and Shivangi, a resident of Magarwara, Unnao, checked into the hotel on Saturday afternoon at 12:30 PM. Both were staying in room number 106.” At 4 PM, Shivangi's scream was heard from the room. She was screaming, asking someone to give her water. A packet of poison was also recovered from the room. Her husband, Dhiru, said that Shivangi called him after consuming poison and said, "I have consumed poison. Now live happily with the children..." After this, the call was disconnected. After the call was disconnected, Dhiru informed the Unnao police about the matter. Unnao police contacted Kanpur's Collectorganj police based on the location and received information about both of them committing suicide. At the post-mortem house on Sunday evening, relatives of both were repeatedly saying that it had been about 13 years since Shivangi's marriage and she had two children. Digvijay also had a wife and children, but both were so misguided that they first abandoned their spouses and children and ran away. When the police and family members became strict, both decided to die together. If I write a book of my pain, people will be scared of love ACP Kalaktarganj stated that Digvijay, before his death, uploaded a reel with a song from Fatehpur station on his Instagram account. It features the song 'If I write a book of my pain, people will be scared of love'. Along with this, he had written that 'I am going to die'. Just a few hours after uploading this video, Digvijay and Shivangi committed suicide. Not only this, before committing suicide, Digvijay had also posted several crying and painful videos on Instagram. Shivangi was practicing law Digvijay was a coach attendant in the Railways. Shivangi's brother said that after completing her law studies, she was practicing in Unnao Court. But during this time, she somehow came into contact with Digvijay, and their closeness increased to such an extent that, disregarding social shame and decorum, both first ran away from home.

The injured were taken to Kanshiram Hospital. The bodies were sent for post-mortem. According to the police, about eight people were traveling in the Scorpio. The car's speed was over 100 kmph. stories.title: Ram Mandir theft accused's family hides in old mud home:Main house locked; brother says, 'Leave us alone, we're tired of answering'
stories.summary: A low-ranking employee in Uttar Pradesh's Pratapgarh, Avinash Shukla's story reads like a movie script. He appeared to transform his fortunes overnight, acquiring two houses within months leaving villagers stunned. His sudden rise came under scrutiny on June 4, when police recovered ₹20.39 lakh in cash and 1,121 US dollars from his house, raising questions about the source of his wealth. A Dainik Bhaskar team visited Avinash's home in Pratapgarh and found it locked. About 50 metres away, his family was found hiding in a mud house. On seeing the reporters, Avinash's brother became agitated and said, "Please leave us alone. We're exhausted from answering people's questions." His father added that the matter is before the Ayodhya court and any answers would come through the legal process. The visit made two things clear: first, the family no longer wants to face villagers; second, they have grown weary of constant questions following the police raid and Avinash's arrest. Read our special ground report... Locals say Avinash's family has disputes with many Nariawan village is about 40 km from Pratapgarh district headquarters. A narrow road through the fields leads to Avinash's house in Babupur. When our team tried to talk to the villagers on camera, they said, “Why do you make us fight? Many people in the village already have disputes with Avinash's family.” People said Avinash's father Ram Sajeevan is a farmer. His family owns about 13 bighas of land. Avinash is the youngest of five brothers. Three elder brothers -- Lalit, Amit, and Anuj -- do farming work at home. Dhaba, shop all closed, family running on farming Money for running Avinash's household came only from farming. Elder brothers Lalit and Amit together opened a dhaba on the road from Fatehpur to Kanpur. But, it had to be closed down in a short time. Lalit then opened a paan shop outside the village. This also did not run well. So, it also had to be closed. Due to the family's financial hardship, Abhishek, Avinash's elder brother, went to Ayodhya about 10 years ago. He was living in Shyam Sadhanalaya Yoga Center in Kaushalpuri. There he served Dr. Chaitanya Guru. Then he became a teacher in his yoga center. Avinash left studies, started selling shoes Avinash's mind was not in his studies. He had dropped out after 10th grade. Derwa market is about 15 kilometers away from home. Avinash started working at a shoe store there. He used to get ₹5,000. However, after working for some time, he left it all. He started insisting to his family to get him an e-rickshaw, which he would drive in the city. But the family did not have enough money to get Avinash an e-rickshaw. Elder brother called him to Ayodhya, got him a job in the temple Avinash told his elder brother Abhishek about his problem. A year and a half ago, he called Avinash to a yoga center in Ayodhya. He recommended Avinash to some people and got him a job at the Ram Temple. This was the opportunity that changed the family's fortune. Manoj Shukla, former Block Head of Babaganj, says, “We don't know this family directly. It's true that until two years ago, this family had nothing. They had opened a paan shop here, which didn't work out. When the theft was exposed, we found out. It seems like a small-scale theft, like a pinch of salt in the dal. But, the big fish hasn't been caught yet.” Family misleading by locking the permanent house from inside Understanding the village atmosphere, our Dainik Bhaskar team reached the place where Avinash's house is located. This white-colored house had a channel gate for entry. It was locked from the inside. No one came out when called. About 50 meters away is a mud house. This is where Avinash's father and his entire family used to live. We reached there. Here we met Avinash's father, brother Amit, and their mother. They flared up as soon as they saw us. They said, “We don't want to talk. The matter is in Ayodhya Court, go there.” Amit said, “I know that some people from the village itself are calling the media from outside and defaming us. Leave from here immediately... otherwise it won't be good.” We explained that they should present their side. Another house built in two years, all facilities available here A new house is being built about 50 meters away from this old house. Villagers said that Avinash is building this house. Some laborers were present in this house, who were making the floor. The house has gates on 3 sides. The entire house has tiles. Indian and Western toilets are also built. This means that all the necessary things should be present here. Villagers say this house was completely ready in just two years. Stealing where we bow our heads is wrong Ram Bahadur from the same village says, “Offerings should not have been stolen from Ram Temple. In the temple where we go, where we bow our heads, if theft is happening there, it's not a good thing.” We asked if the accused of theft is from his own village, Ram Bahadur replied, “We don't have information about this.” Elder son's wedding was normal, second son's had a grand function We asked the villagers - a picture of Avinash's elder brother Amit had surfaced. In it, he was seen standing with lakhs of rupees in his hand. People said this picture was from the time of his wedding. Amit got married on February 25. It is said that Avinash spent about ₹6 lakh on this function. The wedding took place at Ram Janaki Guest House in Lalganj Ajhara. Many videos related to weddings and Haldi have surfaced. A villager attending the wedding says - the first son's wedding didn't have a good function. But, the second son's wedding was very grand. Bought a second-hand Brezza, told friends - enjoy yourselves Avinash bought an old Brezza car last year. The car cost ₹3.5 lakh. He used to travel to and from the village in this car. He would throw parties for his friends in the village. He spent a lot of money. If friends asked him to get them a job like his, he would say, “You guys eat and drink, tell me where you need something... don't try to know more than that.” ₹2.5 lakh transferred to Avinash's girlfriend's account After the arrest, discussions quickly arose that Avinash's marriage had broken off. After reaching the village, it came to light that Avinash also has a girlfriend in Ayodhya. Avinash had gifted her an iPhone. He had transferred ₹2.5 lakh to her bank account. He often used to gift her jewelry. Police also found 11 grams of gold and 375 grams of silver jewelry from Avinash's house. When the police interrogated Avinash, he admitted all this. The police have not yet questioned that girl. Villagers say that there is no information about his relationship with any girl in Pratapgarh. Ayodhya Yoga Center expelled Avinash's brother As soon as Avinash's name came up in the Ram Mandir offering theft case, Shyam Sadhanalaya Yoga Center expelled Avinash's brother Abhishek from there. Police investigated this yoga center in Kaushalpuri multiple times. From here, on June 28, a box labeled 'Ramrajya Kosh' was also found. It had a Paytm QR code on it. Several documents related to Ram Mandir were also found. So far, the investigation has revealed that theft of ₹60 lakh to ₹70 lakh was committed solely by Avinash. stories.title: UP transfers 182 PCS officers overnight:54 women among them; Deepika Meher posted as Shamli SDM, Lavgeet Kaur sent to Noida
stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, 182 Provincial Civil Service (PCS) officers were transferred late on Sunday night. Among them are 54 women officers. Under the order issued by the government, Sub-Divisional Magistrates (SDMs) of several tehsils have been changed, while some officers have been given new responsibilities. According to the order, Surabhi Sharma, SDM of Kanpur Dehat, has been sent to Baghpat, Pushpendra Patel, SDM of Ghazipur, to Ambedkar Nagar, and Shubham Yadav, SDM of Unnao, to Bulandshahr. Pratibha Mishra, SDM of Varanasi, has been posted to Kanpur Dehat, Gopal Sharma, SDM of Mainpuri, to Bareilly, and Mithlesh Kumar Tiwari, SDM of Raebareli, to Mainpuri. Lavgeet Kaur, SDM of Hathras, has been made Officer on Special Duty (OSD) in Greater Noida Authority, while Pushpnath Chaudhary, SDM of Amroha, has been sent to Unnao. Devendra Pratap Singh, posted in Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA), has been made SDM of Jhansi. Additionally, Pragya Pandey, SDM of Hasanganj tehsil of Unnao, has been sent to Barabanki, Ajendra Singh from Kaushambi to Unnao, and Abhinav Yadav from Misrikh tehsil of Sitapur to Jalaun. Meanwhile, Akanksha Gautam has been made Sub-Divisional Magistrate of Sonbhadra from Sitapur, and Shikha Shukla of Kanpur Nagar from Sitapur. stories.title: Video | CM Yadav inspects Simhastha works on bike:Wears helmet, walks 2 km through Ujjain, makes jalebis during ground reality check
stories.summary: Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav conducted an on-ground inspection of preparations for Simhastha-2028 on Friday evening, setting aside official protocol to tour parts of Ujjain on a motorcycle while wearing a helmet. The Chief Minister later walked nearly 2 kilometres through the city to review ongoing development works, interacted with residents, and issued on-the-spot instructions to officials. During the visit, he also stopped at a familiar sweet shop at Kanthal Square, where he prepared jalebis and shared tea with the shop owner. Motorcycle tour across key development sites After arriving in Ujjain from Nagda on Friday evening, CM Yadav left the Chief Minister's residence on a motorcycle wearing a helmet. He inspected ongoing infrastructure and development projects across several locations, including: The inspection focused on works related to preparations for Simhastha-2028, one of the country's largest religious congregations. See these pictures Walks 2 km, interacts with residents After reviewing construction work at Freeganj Bridge and Medicity, the Chief Minister walked nearly 2 kilometres from Koyla Phatak to Kanthal Square. During the walk, he assessed road widening projects and other Simhastha-related infrastructure works, interacted with local residents, and issued directions to officials to expedite pending work. Residents welcomed him at several points along the route. Stops at old acquaintance's sweet shop At Kanthal Square, the Chief Minister visited a jalebi shop owned by an old acquaintance. He prepared jalebis himself, ordered tea, and drank warm water while interacting with the shop owner. Yadav said he had been associated with the shop since his days in student politics. 'Wanted to see the ground reality myself' Speaking to the media, the Chief Minister said preparations for Simhastha-2028 are progressing rapidly. He said the state government is strengthening roads, traffic management, and civic infrastructure to accommodate the expected influx of millions of devotees during the religious event. Explaining his decision to inspect the city on a motorcycle and on foot, Yadav said the objective was to personally assess the actual progress of development works on the ground. He also noted that after the development of the Mahakal Mahalok corridor, religious tourism in Ujjain has increased significantly, contributing to the state's economy and creating more employment opportunities.

stories.title: Google alert leads to man's arrest for recording obscene clips:Police say accused secretly filmed minor girls' private moments
stories.summary: A man has been arrested in Kanpur in a child sexual abuse material (CSAM) case after Google alerted the police about suspected illegal content stored on his Google Drive. According to police, the accused allegedly secretly recorded explicit videos of his minor cousins and other girls from his neighbourhood, uploaded the files to Google Drive, and stored them there. Following a digital alert received from Google, police tracked him using his IMEI number and IP address. The accused was arrested on Friday, and police said 15 objectionable videos involving minor girls were recovered from his phone and cloud storage. Investigators are also examining whether any of the videos were shared or uploaded to other online platforms. The case falls under the Chaman Ganj police station limits in Kanpur. Google alert triggered investigation Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Crime) Anjali Vishwakarma said the Cyber Crime Police Station received information on July 6 through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP) regarding a serious offence involving women and children. Following the alert, two cyber investigation teams launched a confidential probe. Google shared digital information related to the account, enabling investigators to identify the suspect and proceed with the investigation. Accused traced through digital evidence Police said Google provided several technical details, including: Using this information, investigators identified and arrested the accused from the Chaman Ganj area. According to police, the accused is a high school graduate who works in the baby diaper business. Investigators said he had deleted the videos from his mobile phone but stored them in Google Drive, where Google's automated safety systems flagged the content. During questioning, the accused allegedly admitted that he had been secretly recording videos for the past three months. Videos allegedly included minor family members Police alleged that the accused secretly recorded explicit videos of: Some videos were allegedly recorded without the victims' knowledge, including while they were in private spaces. Police said around 15 objectionable videos have been recovered so far. Investigators also revealed that the National Center for Missing Exploited Children (NCMEC) had generated four cyber tipline reports related to the accused's account. During the investigation, police also found information linked to three additional complaints. Police investigating possible online distribution Police are now examining whether the recovered videos were merely stored in cloud storage or were also uploaded or distributed through other websites or online platforms. Digital forensic analysis of the accused's devices and online accounts is currently underway. How Google detects such content Police explained that many users store personal files on Google Drive, but the platform also uses automated safety systems and technical tools to identify content that violates its policies. If uploaded files are detected as suspected Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) or other prohibited content, Google's systems may flag the account. In accordance with legal requirements, Google may share relevant information with law enforcement agencies, including: This information helps investigators identify suspects and pursue criminal cases. Content prohibited on Google Drive Under Google's policies and applicable law, users are prohibited from storing or sharing content such as: The investigation is ongoing, and police are continuing to examine the accused's digital activity to determine the full extent of the alleged offences.

stories.title: Lucknow City Health Officer takes charge:Focuses on waterlogging and communicable disease control, reviews preparedness with sanitation and food officials
stories.summary: Newly appointed Municipal Health Officer (MHO) Ashish Kumar Singh on Friday formally assumed charge at the Lucknow Municipal Corporation headquarters and held his first review meeting with Zonal Sanitary Officers (ZSOs) and Sanitary and Food Inspectors (SFIs). During the meeting, Singh instructed officials to carry out their responsibilities with seriousness and accountability. He reviewed key civic issues, including sanitation, waterlogging, communicable disease control, fogging operations, drainage maintenance, and disposal of public grievances. Special monitoring of waterlogging-prone areas The Municipal Health Officer sought detailed information on identified waterlogging hotspots across the city. He directed officials to maintain close surveillance in vulnerable areas and ensure immediate response during heavy rainfall. Field officers were also instructed to regularly monitor ground conditions and promptly report updates to senior authorities. Warning for unauthorised absence Emphasising accountability, Singh instructed officials to issue warnings to employees found absent without valid justification. He also directed supervisory officers to closely monitor the attendance and performance of staff working under their jurisdiction. Daily field inspections made mandatory All Zonal Sanitary Officers and Sanitary Food Inspectors have been instructed to conduct daily field inspections in their respective areas. The Municipal Health Officer stressed that the actual condition of sanitation services can only be assessed through on-site inspections rather than office-based reviews. Any deficiencies identified during inspections must be rectified without delay. Accelerate communicable disease control campaign Reviewing the city's communicable disease prevention campaign, Singh directed officials to intensify operations, particularly in identified disease hotspots. He asked officials to ensure daily action in vulnerable areas and submit regular reports on progress to facilitate effective monitoring. Coordination on drainage issues The meeting also discussed problems related to major drains across the city. Singh instructed officials that issues falling outside the Health Department's jurisdiction should immediately be referred to the concerned departments. Any open drains or drainage-related hazards must be reported without delay so corrective action can be initiated. Officials' concerns heard The Municipal Health Officer also interacted with Zonal Sanitary Officers and Food Inspectors to understand operational challenges faced during fieldwork. He assured them that practical issues affecting their work would be addressed through appropriate administrative measures. He further directed that a meeting with agencies responsible for sanitation services be held within the next week to strengthen accountability and improve cleanliness across the city. Regular fogging across all zones Officials have been instructed to carry out fogging operations regularly based on local requirements. Singh said that any shortage of fogging machines, fuel or other resources should be resolved immediately in coordination with the concerned agencies to ensure uninterrupted operations. He also directed all implementing agencies to maintain adequate manpower, equipment and other resources so that sanitation work is not affected. Time-bound disposal of public complaints The Municipal Health Officer instructed officials to ensure 100% time-bound disposal of all complaints related to sanitation, waterlogging, fogging and public health received through any platform. He also directed that details of action taken and complaint resolution must be promptly shared with the municipal war room to ensure continuous monitoring and accountability.

stories.title: UP's district panchayat chiefs become administrators for first time:Government bars them from taking major decisions as appointments await High Court ruling
stories.summary: In a first for Uttar Pradesh, the Yogi Adityanath government has appointed the existing chairpersons of all 75 district Panchayats as administrators after the completion of their constitutional tenure, allowing them to continue in office until fresh panchayat elections are held. The official order was issued on Friday, a day before the current tenure of all district panchayat chairpersons ends on July 11. Ordinarily, after the expiry of a district panchayat's term, the District Magistrate (DM) is appointed as administrator. However, under the new order, the elected chairpersons will remain in charge in an administrative capacity. Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar confirmed that the government has formally entrusted the district panchayat chairpersons with the role of administrators. No Major Policy Decisions, Routine Administration to Continue Although the chairpersons will continue to head their respective district panchayats, the government has imposed certain restrictions on their powers to avoid legal and procedural complications. As administrators, they will not be permitted to take major policy decisions, but they will continue to oversee: Official work will continue under their signatures until the newly elected bodies assume office. First such decision in Uttar Pradesh This is the first time in Uttar Pradesh that elected district panchayat chairpersons have been appointed as administrators after the expiry of their constitutional term instead of handing over charge to bureaucrats. The move comes as panchayat elections in the state have been delayed due to pending legal proceedings. Government's strategic objectives The decision is widely seen as serving multiple administrative and political objectives. BJP retains administrative presence in most districts Of the state's 75 district panchayats, 68 are currently headed by BJP-backed chairpersons, allowing the ruling party to retain its presence in district-level governance until elections are held. Avoiding complete bureaucratic control Had District Magistrates been appointed as administrators, elected representatives would have had no role in district panchayat administration. The new arrangement ensures that existing chairpersons continue to function as local administrative heads. Maintaining organisational strength ahead of elections With the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections approaching, the continuation of district panchayat chairpersons is expected to help the ruling party maintain its organisational network and outreach in rural areas. Why the government took this decision According to the government, the move was intended to: What happens next? The new administrative arrangement will take effect immediately after the chairpersons' tenure expires on July 11. Meanwhile, the issue remains under judicial scrutiny. The government's earlier decision to appoint gram pradhans as administrators has already been challenged before the Allahabad High Court, with the next hearing scheduled for July 13. The High Court's observations in that case could have implications for the district panchayat arrangement as well.

stories.title: Rajbhar blames Akhilesh for Panchayat poll delay:Minister says, 'Govt was ready for elections'; claims 'Islam teaches hatred'
stories.summary: Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) chief and Uttar Pradesh Cabinet Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar blamed the Samajwadi Party (SP) for the delay in the state's Panchayat elections, alleging that legal action initiated by the party stalled the poll process. Addressing the media on Friday in Ambedkar Nagar at 2 pm, Rajbhar claimed the Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath-led government had completed all preparations to conduct the elections on time. "The Panchayati Raj Department had completed all necessary preparations and procedures. We were ready to conduct the elections, but a petition filed by Akhilesh Yadav's legal cell advisor in the High Court delayed the process," he said. 'Government was prepared, court case delayed polls' Rajbhar said the Allahabad High Court subsequently summoned both the Uttar Pradesh government and the State Election Commission after the petition was filed. According to him, the government submitted timely responses to all the court's queries and remains prepared to hold the elections once legal issues are resolved. High Court to hear matter again on July 13 The minister said that, following earlier directions from the High Court, the government had constituted a Backward Classes Commission to comply with legal requirements related to panchayat elections. He added that after administrators were appointed in place of village heads (Gram Pradhans), objections were raised against that decision as well. Rajbhar said the High Court has now summoned the government again on July 13, seeking an explanation for appointing administrators in place of elected village heads. "The ball is now entirely in the High Court's court. Whatever directions the court gives after the July 13 hearing, the government will act accordingly," he said. Remarks on Sanatan and Islam Rajbhar also made remarks comparing Sanatan Dharma and Islam. He said Sanatan Dharma promotes brotherhood, harmony and social unity, while alleging that Islam teaches hatred. He further accused Akhilesh Yadav of previously practising "politics centred around Islam" and claimed that the SP leader has recently begun speaking about Sanatan Dharma because of changing political circumstances. Fresh attack on Akhilesh Yadav Continuing his criticism of the Samajwadi Party chief, Rajbhar repeated an earlier allegation that party workers had told him money was demanded from people seeking to meet Akhilesh Yadav. He said he had earlier posted about the allegation on social media platform X after receiving complaints. Comments on socialism and PDA Referring to socialist leader Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia, Rajbhar said a "true socialist" does not use caste identifiers with his or her name. He questioned why Akhilesh Yadav continues to use a caste surname if he truly believes in socialist principles. The minister also criticised the Samajwadi Party's PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) political plank, alleging that its leaders frequently change the meaning of the acronym and make inconsistent statements. Criticism of previous Samajwadi governments Rajbhar also accused previous Samajwadi Party governments in Uttar Pradesh of fostering an atmosphere of lawlessness, alleging that their tenures were marked by incidents of crime, looting and murder. The Panchayat election matter remains pending before the Allahabad High Court, with the next hearing scheduled for July 13.

stories.title: Grandfather dies saving grandson from electrocution:Child's iron rod touched high-tension line as he tried to retrieve kite
stories.summary: A 65-year-old man died of electrocution while trying to save his 12-year-old grandson, who came into contact with an 11,000-volt high-tension power line while attempting to retrieve a kite from an electricity pole using an iron rod. The incident occurred around 12 pm on Friday in the Khurja area of Bulandshahr. The injured boy is undergoing treatment at a higher medical centre. A video of the incident has also surfaced. Kite got stuck in electricity pole According to police, Ahad (12) had gone to his grandfather's house in Burj Usman village to play. While flying a kite on the rooftop, the kite became entangled in an electricity pole carrying an 11 kV high-tension line. The boy attempted to retrieve it using an iron rod, which came into contact with the power line. The current passed through the rod, electrocuting him. Witnesses said sparks and smoke erupted from the pole as the child caught fire and began screaming in pain. First 2 pictures Grandfather dies while trying to save him Seeing his grandson in distress, Israr (65) rushed to rescue him. He tried to pull the boy away with his bare hands, but was himself struck by the powerful electric current. The child was thrown away from the point of contact, while Israr collapsed unconscious. Family members rushed both of them to the hospital. Doctors declared Israr dead on arrival, while Ahad, who suffered critical injuries, was referred to a higher medical facility, where he remains under treatment. Police confirm electrocution Khurja Station House Officer Ramphal Singh said the elderly man died while trying to save the child after he came into contact with the high-voltage line. Police have sent the body for post-mortem examination. Further action will be taken after the report is received, the officer said. Family background Ahad's father, Abrar (35), works at a pottery manufacturing unit. The family lives in Burj Usman village. Ahad studies in Class 3 at a private school and has two younger siblings. According to the family, he had gone to visit his grandfather when the fatal accident occurred.

stories.title: Fake MLM racket busted, 300 job seekers rescued:₹50 lakh extorted through bogus network marketing scheme; 19 arrested
stories.summary: Varanasi Police have busted a large-scale fake multi-level marketing (MLM) and pyramid scheme, rescuing around 300 unemployed youths who were allegedly confined and pressured to recruit more people into the network after paying hefty registration fees. The operation was carried out on Thursday after police raided a three-storey building in the Rohania police station area. Following interrogation, 19 people were arrested in connection with the racket. Police also seized 20 mobile phones and two luxury cars from the accused. Victims lured with fake job offers DCP (Crime) Neetu Kadyan said the gang was operating under the guise of a corporate office and running an illegal MLM and pyramid marketing network. The accused allegedly contacted unemployed youths from Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and other states, offering office jobs, Tata company jobs and agricultural work with a promised salary of ₹25,000 per month. After being brought to Varanasi, the victims were made to attend fake interviews in what appeared to be a corporate office. They were then asked to pay ₹30,000–35,000 as registration or joining fees. In return, they were handed a basic kit containing low-value items such as clothes, oil and soap worth only ₹1,000–2,000. Brainwashed into expanding the network According to police, the victims were subsequently shifted to a training centre where they were allegedly subjected to psychological manipulation. The recruits were promised a luxurious lifestyle and pressured to bring at least three new members into the network. They were allegedly threatened that if they failed to recruit others, they would neither receive salaries nor get refunds of the money they had paid. Gang operated through fake companies Police said the accused were operating under a fake company named Mahadev Enterprises and had obtained a franchise of an MLM firm called Royal Health Wellness Private Limited to lend legitimacy to their activities. The operation allegedly functioned as an organised cyber-enabled recruitment fraud targeting unemployed youth across multiple states. Gang leader identified, financial probe underway ACP (Crime) Vidush Saxena identified the alleged kingpin as Deepak Kumar Shah, a resident of Jamui district in Bihar. Police said preliminary examination of his State Bank of India (SBI) and HDFC Bank accounts revealed around ₹4 crore in credits over the past year. Investigators also found: Police said a detailed financial investigation is underway to determine the full scale of the racket. 19 arrested Police arrested the following accused: Police said further investigation is in progress to identify additional victims, trace the money trail and determine whether more people were involved in operating the network.

stories.summary: Anandiben Patel – उत्तरप्रदेश की गवर्नर आनंदीबेन पटेल के एक बयान पर बवाल मच गया है। उन्होंने एक कार्यक्रम में प्रेम विवाह, भागते प्रेमी जोड़ों और पढ़ाई के दौरान युवतियों की प्रेग्नेंसी पर कमेंट किए। गवर्नर आनंदीबेन पटेल का कार्यक्रम का यह वीडियो वायरल हो गया जिससे पॉलिटिकल विवाद खड़ा हो गया है। सोशल मीडिया में उनके बयान पर तीखी प्रतिक्रिया व्यक्त की जा रही है। गवर्नर आनंदीबेन पटेल के कमेंट्स, उत्तरप्रदेश सहित देशभर में पॉलिटिकल सर्कल के बीच बहस का विषय बन गए हैं। आलोचकों का कहना है कि उन्होंने जिस एकेडमिक इवेंट में ये बातें कहीं, वह कार्यक्रम स्टूडेंट्स की अचीवमेंट को सेलिब्रेट करने के लिए रखा गया था। कांग्रेस के वरिष्ठ नेता टीएस सिंह देव ने कहा कि, “यह बालिग़ पुरुषों और महिलाओं के बीच के रिश्तों का मामला है। मेरी राय में, सामाजिक ढांचे के भीतर, आम तौर पर शादी के बाद ही गर्भधारण होना चाहिए। गर्भवती होना एक बात है, लेकिन पैदा होने वाले बच्चे को सामाजिक माहौल में अलग नज़रिए से देखा जाएगा।” लगातार हो रही आलोचना के बाद गर्वनर आनंदीबेन पटेल ने सफाई भी दी। उन्होंने स्पष्ट किया कि उनका मकसद लव मैरिज का विरोध करना नहीं था।

stories.title: Gorakhpur District Hospital launches Dengue prevention campaign:Health dept on alert amid monsoon, urges weekly 'Dry Day'
stories.summary: With the risk of dengue expected to rise during the monsoon season, the Gorakhpur Health Department has stepped up preventive measures across the city. As part of the initiative, a special Dengue Prevention Drive was conducted at the District Hospital campus on Thursday at 2 PM. During the campaign, extensive cleanliness activities were carried out within the hospital premises and surrounding areas. Waterlogging spots were identified, anti-larval chemicals were sprayed, and people were educated about measures to prevent dengue. Multi-department campaign led by senior health officials The drive was conducted under the leadership of Chief Medical Officer (CMO) Dr Rajesh Jha and Chief Medical Superintendent Dr OP Singh. Teams from the Health Department, Malaria Department, Filaria Department, and the Municipal Corporation jointly participated in the operation. Accumulated water found inside the hospital campus was immediately removed, while anti-larval treatment was carried out at locations prone to mosquito breeding. Healthcare workers and hospital staff were also sensitised about dengue prevention measures. Dengue mosquito breeds in clean, stagnant water: CMO According to the CMO Dr Rajesh Jha, the Aedes mosquito, which transmits dengue, breeds rapidly in clean and stagnant water. He urged residents to ensure that water does not collect in their homes, on rooftops, or in surrounding areas. And stressed that awareness and preventive precautions are more effective than medicines in controlling the spread of dengue. Residents urged to observe a weekly 'Dry Day' District Malaria Officer Angad Singh appealed to residents to observe a 'Dry Day' at least once every week. He advised people to completely empty and clean coolers, flower pots, refrigerator trays, overhead water tanks, buckets, and other water storage containers once a week. According to him, this simple practice prevents mosquito breeding and significantly reduces the risk of dengue transmission. Anti-dengue campaigns to continue across the district The campaign was attended by Medical Superintendent Dr BK Suman, Senior Consultant Dr Rajesh, Quality Manager Dr Mukul, along with doctors, healthcare workers, and teams from the Municipal Corporation, Malaria Department, and Filaria Department. Officials said that, in addition to the ongoing "Dengue-Free Hostel Campaign," similar dengue prevention drives will continue at hospitals, government institutions, and other public places across the district to protect people from mosquito-borne diseases during the rainy season.

stories.title: Man gets death sentence for killing 1.5-year-old boy:Convict pressured child's mother to marry him; slammed toddler to ground 8 times
stories.summary: A court in Firozabad has sentenced a man to death for the brutal murder of an 18-month-old boy, whom he allegedly killed after the child's mother rejected his repeated marriage proposal. The verdict was delivered on Friday at 2:45 pm, nearly one month and 10 days after the crime. The child was murdered in Shikohabad on 30, and CCTV footage of the incident had also surfaced. It showed the accused killing the child. Police later arrested the accused after shooting him in both legs. Court delivers verdict in just over a month Government counsel Rajeev Priyadarshi said the court pronounced its judgment within one month and 10 days of the incident. Police filed the chargesheet within six days of the murder. During the trial, the defence argued that the accused was mentally unstable at the time of the incident. However, the court rejected the claim and held Viraj alias Jitendra Pathak guilty. According to the prosecutor, CCTV footage proved to be the most critical piece of evidence. When the footage was played in court, the accused reportedly began slapping himself and appeared visibly distressed. The prosecution said the speedy conviction would strengthen public confidence in the justice system. Background: Marriage proposal rejected According to police and the victim's family, the child's mother, Rati Sharma, had married Suneet, a resident of Badaun, about three years ago. However, the couple had been facing marital disputes, and Rati had been staying with her mother. The accused, Viraj, who is the son of Suneet's aunt from Shekhupur in Badaun, had allegedly been pressuring Rati to marry him despite knowing she was already married. Her family said she repeatedly rejected his proposal, after which he became angry. Toddler lured away on the pretext of buying candy On May 30, Rati had gone with her mother, daughter and her 18-month-old son Aarav to visit a friend, Pushplata Pathak, who had recently been injured in a road accident. Viraj also arrived at the house that afternoon. According to investigators, he took Aarav away on the pretext of buying him candy. After reaching a deserted lane, he allegedly smashed the child onto the ground eight times, causing fatal head injuries. He later returned carrying the unconscious child, left him outside the house and fled. Family members rushed Aarav to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. CCTV captured the murder Police examined CCTV cameras installed near the crime scene, which allegedly showed the accused repeatedly throwing the child onto the ground. The footage became the prosecution's strongest evidence during the trial. Following the incident, police tracked down the accused. During an alleged encounter, he sustained bullet injuries to both legs before being arrested. Mother says, 'My child's neck was hanging' Rati said, "My in-laws used to assault me, and I was often unwell. Because of this, my mother brought me back to live with her. After some time, Viraj, the son of my husband's aunt, started calling me. One day, he said he was coming to meet me and proposed marriage. I refused, telling him I was already married and had a child." "Viraj came to my aunt's house and took my son Aarav with him on the pretext of buying him a toffee. Since he was a relative, I had no reason to suspect him." She alleged that Viraj took Aarav a short distance away and repeatedly slammed him to the ground, killing him. "My child's neck was completely limp," she said. According to police, the accused allegedly slammed the child onto the ground eight times, causing fatal head injuries. He then carried Aarav back in his arms, left him outside the house, and fled. When family members found the child, they rushed him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Police later examined CCTV footage from the area, which allegedly showed Viraj assaulting the child. He was subsequently arrested after police shot him in both legs during an encounter. Speedy investigation led to conviction District Government Counsel Rajeev Priyadarshi said the police and prosecution pursued the case swiftly. The prosecution completed the examination of 13 witnesses in a short period, and the court convicted the accused based on strong eyewitness testimony, forensic evidence and the CCTV footage. The court ultimately awarded the death penalty for what it considered a rare and brutal crime.

stories.title: UP to plant 35 crore saplings on July 12:CM Yogi to launch drive from Gorakhpur under 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' theme
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government will undertake a massive plantation drive on July 12, aiming to plant 35 crore saplings in a single day across the state. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will launch the campaign by planting a sapling near the Link Expressway in Sahjanwa, Gorakhpur. The drive will be carried out with the participation of the Forest Department, 26 government departments, and the general public. Announcing the initiative at a press conference at the Forest Headquarters on Friday, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Environment, Forest, Zoological Parks and Climate Change Arun Kumar Saxena said the campaign is intended to transform tree plantation into a people's movement. 'One tree in mother's name' to be the central theme The minister said this year's plantation campaign will be based on the theme "One Tree in Mother's Name", with every sapling dedicated to mothers as a mark of respect and remembrance. To ensure large-scale participation, the government has involved government employees, students, farmers, voluntary organisations, NCC, NSS, the Indian Medical Association (IMA), women's and youth organisations, trade bodies, and farmer producer organisations. Plantation drive to cover rural and urban areas Saplings will be planted across every gram panchayat, urban wards, schools, colleges, universities, medical colleges, hospitals, Krishi Vigyan Kendras, industrial units, power plants, court premises, and along railway lines, expressways, highways, and other major roads. The government has also given special emphasis to the participation of school students. Special green zones to be developed As part of the campaign, the state will develop several themed green zones, including: The government will also undertake eco-restoration of 36 mythological forests in Mathura. To improve nutrition and health among economically weaker families, drumstick (moringa) and mango saplings will also be distributed and planted. Millions of saplings along expressways The state government plans to plant saplings on vacant land along both sides of all expressways in Uttar Pradesh. Along the Ganga Expressway, currently under construction between Prayagraj and Meerut, around 550,000 saplings will be planted across 500 hectares. Species selected for the campaign include Peepal, Banyan, Pakar, Cluster Fig, Neem, Shisham, Mango, Jamun, Mahua, Tamarind, Drumstick, Gulmohar, and Jacaranda, among other varieties suited to the local climate. Ministers, judges and public representatives to participate Besides Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, both Deputy Chief Ministers, Union Ministers, state ministers, Members of Parliament, MLAs, High Court judges, chairpersons of various commissions, and other public representatives will participate in plantation drives across different districts. District-level committees headed by District Magistrates have been constituted to oversee preparations. 57.62 crore saplings ready for plantation According to the government, 57.62 crore high-quality saplings are available across 2,600 nurseries managed by the Forest Department, other government agencies, and the private sector. The government also claimed that Uttar Pradesh's green cover has increased by 338,000 acres over the past nine years. During the same period, the state's forest carbon stock has risen by 2.46%, higher than the national average of 1.13%, according to official data.

stories.title: CM Yogi begins three-day Gorakhpur visit:To inaugurate and lay foundation stones for 11 projects worth ₹1,018 crore
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath arrived in Gorakhpur on Friday for a three-day visit, during which he will review development works, assess the law and order situation, inaugurate and lay foundation stones for projects worth ₹1,018 crore, and launch the state's plantation campaign. The Chief Minister reached the Gorakhnath Temple at around 2:20 pm, where he offered prayers to Guru Gorakhnath and paid tribute at the Samadhi of his spiritual mentor, the late Mahant Avaidyanath. On the first day of his visit, Yogi is expected to hold a review meeting with officials to assess ongoing development works and the law and order situation in the district. ₹1,018 crore worth of projects to be launched On Saturday, the Chief Minister will inaugurate and lay foundation stones for 11 development projects worth a total of ₹1,018 crore. The programme includes: Bhathat-Banssthan four-lane road to be inaugurated CM Yogi will reach Bhathat at around 4:30 pm on Saturday to inaugurate the 11.6-km Bhathat-Banssthan four-lane road. The road serves as the main approach to Uttar Pradesh's first Ayush University and has been developed with proper drainage facilities on both sides. After the road inauguration, the Chief Minister will visit the Ayush University, where he will inaugurate development works, including two hostels, and review the university's ongoing infrastructure projects. Foundation stones for seven new projects Following his visit to the university, the Chief Minister will offer prayers at the Vamant Mata Temple before participating in a public programme. During the event, he will inaugurate additional road projects and lay foundation stones for seven new development projects, all linked to the Pipraich Assembly constituency. Will meet families of deceased industrialists During his visit, Yogi Adityanath is also expected to visit the families of late industrialist Om Prakash Jalan, businessman Bal Krishna Bajaj, and the family of the mother of Geeta Press trustee Devidayal Agrawal to offer condolences. Statewide plantation campaign to begin from Gorakhpur The Chief Minister will launch the state's plantation campaign beginning July 12 from Gorakhpur. He will plant saplings near the Bhagwanpur Toll Plaza on the Gorakhpur Link Expressway and later address a public gathering. Road projects to be inaugurated The Chief Minister will inaugurate the following road projects: Bhathat-Banssthan four-lane road Chakjalal–Ghoda Deur–Tarkulahi Hanuman Temple link road Hafiz Nagar second link road Pipraich Bargadahi road to Sirsiya Mahadev Temple Projects for which foundation stones will be laid The Chief Minister will lay foundation stones for the following projects:

stories.title: 'You too can shed crocodile tears, who's stopping you?':Chandrashekhar hits back after Mayawati accused him of exploiting violence for political gain
stories.summary: Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad on Friday hit back at BSP chief Mayawati, responding to her criticism over protests and allegations of political opportunism. Addressing reporters in Meerut at around 4 pm, Chandrashekhar said, You say we come only to shed crocodile tears. You can come and shed crocodile tears too. Who is stopping you? Without naming Mayawati directly, he also rejected her advice that victims should seek justice only through the courts. "She says people should go to the courts, even the Supreme Court, for justice. But justice can take 10 years. Should our sisters and daughters continue to suffer while we remain silent?" he said. Earlier in the day, BSP president Mayawati, without naming Chandrashekhar, accused certain organisations and political parties of misleading Dalits and other marginalised communities for narrow political interests by encouraging protests that lead to violence and road blockades. She said such actions do not deliver justice and only worsen the hardships faced by victims. 'Political power is the master key' Mayawati reiterated that Dr. B.R. Ambedkar had empowered Dalits through the right to vote, but said that merely having voting rights was not enough. She asserted that Scheduled Castes and other deprived sections must secure the "master key" of political power at both the Centre and in the states to fully benefit from their constitutional rights. According to her, BSP founder Kanshi Ram established the party with this very objective. Fight within the framework of the constitution The BSP chief stressed that every struggle against injustice or caste discrimination must remain within the constitutional and legal framework. Referring to Dr. Ambedkar's teachings, she said people should seek justice through the judicial process, moving from lower courts to the Supreme Court if necessary, as the Constitution provides adequate legal remedies. 'Street protests are not the solution' Mayawati criticised repeated protests and demonstrations, citing incidents in Meerut, Saharanpur, Prayagraj, Hardoi and other places. She alleged that certain organisations and political parties were misleading vulnerable communities into staging protests that often escalate into violence, clashes and road blockades. According to her, such actions create more difficulties rather than resolving the underlying issues. 'Leaders gain politically, victims continue to suffer' The former Chief Minister said violence, public unrest and road blockades only worsen the situation for victims. She claimed that while political leaders use such incidents to strengthen their own position, the affected families do not receive justice and instead face greater hardship. Mayawati urged people to remain united and use the strength of their vote to achieve political power, describing it as the only lasting solution to the problems faced by marginalised communities. Appeal ahead of upcoming elections With Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections and local body polls approaching, Mayawati cautioned people against being influenced by political parties and organisations that become active during election season. She urged voters to remain vigilant and not fall prey to attempts aimed at provoking unrest for electoral gains. Background: Meerut protest Mayawati's remarks came against the backdrop of the Meerut case involving Lalita Gautam, who went missing on May 15. Her body was recovered in the Rohta area on May 17. Police arrested the main accused on May 18 and later detained another person for allegedly helping destroy evidence. On July 8, people associated with the Bhim Army allegedly joined the victim's family in a protest outside the District Magistrate's office. According to police, demonstrators staged an unauthorised road blockade, attempted to force their way through the DM office gate and clashed with police. The protest lasted nearly six hours, during which two ambulances were reportedly stranded in traffic. Stone-pelting left 11 police personnel injured. Police later arrested seven people and registered FIRs against more than 30 individuals. Saharanpur incident Mayawati also referred to a caste clash that took place around two months ago in Lalwala village in Saharanpur's Deoband area over a land dispute and the installation of an idol. The confrontation involved members of the Thakur and Dalit communities. Following the incident, MP Chandrashekhar Azad and his party had staged protests demanding action.

stories.title: Inspector caught on camera demanding ₹1,50,000 bribe:Promises to not take action in bank fraud case; cop suspended
stories.summary: Allegations have been made against Inspector Guddu Prasad, posted at Rahimabad police station in Lucknow, for demanding a bribe of ₹1.5 lakh. A video of this has surfaced, in which he is demanding this amount in exchange for protecting the accused in the investigation of a case. In the video, he is saying, “If I get this much money, then I will also write that the accused was not found at home. I will not try to search.” After the video surfaced, the inspector was suspended. Action was taken against the inspector on the night of July 9 at around 8:30 pm. He was investigating a case of bank fraud. In exchange for protecting the accused's family members for recovery, he finalised the bribe with a middleman outside the police station. The middleman recorded a video of this inside the police station itself. Read what's in the video In the video, victim Vishnu Kumar is seen sitting inside the police station. Inspector Guddu Prasad is in front of him, who is not visible in the beginning of the video. Inspector- Instead of 10, you will have to pay 20. The other party will only get 5. (At this, Vishnu Kumar nods his head in agreement.) Middleman- Yes, understood? Come here, I'll explain. (Saying this, the middleman steps outside.) Middleman- Come comfortably in the shade, let's talk. Look Dwivedi ji, this Guddu bhai (Inspector Guddu) not from now, I have very old relations with him. Inspector- Dwivedi ji Middleman (interrupting in between)- One minute. This matter of Santosh Kumar? Who is Santosh Kumar to you? Inspector- Santosh is their elder brother. This is the younger brother. Shubham is their nephew. Their family members live in Alamnagar. If I wanted, I could have dragged them too. Middleman- This is your humanity. Inspector- This is not humanity...I cannot stoop to this level. Middleman- Yes, see. He is of such high character. Vishnu Kumar- We are tense. Inspector- Your tension...What did I tell you? That brother, if you cannot come, then I will come to your house. I said this, right? (At this time the inspector's face is visible in the video. The inspector is in civil dress.) Middleman- Yes. Inspector- ...but that child's statement is necessary because he is the one who filed the missing person report. I will take his statement only. I will also continue it saying that brother has not been found till date. I will not even try to search. I know but still I will not go. This much I can do. Middleman- Get his statement done. What charge will he have to pay? Inspector- That I have told Tariq bhai. It will be the same. Vishnu Kumar- (looks towards the Inspector) Inspector- One fifty Vishnu Kumar- I didn't understand... (says this while looking towards the middleman) Middleman- He is saying one fifty. (Vishnu Kumar looks towards the Inspector again.) Middleman- Tell me how much is it? Inspector- One and a half lakh. Vishnu Kumar- Can't it be reduced? Inspector- Now talk to him (middleman) about it. Middleman- (laughs) Vishnu Kumar- One and a half lakh is too much. Make it one lakh. (The Inspector comes near the middleman and asks in his ear, “Is one lakh too much?” After this he starts whispering.) Inspector- Here I am not an Inspector. Middleman- He is my elder brother. Inspector- He is my younger brother. Middleman- (to Vishnu Kumar) If one lakh rupees cannot be done tomorrow, then do it day after tomorrow. And yes, there should be no politics in this. (to Inspector) Tell him, explain to him that there should be no politics. (to Vishnu Kumar) Bring him and get his statement recorded. Inspector- (to Vishnu Kumar) Bring him within two days and get his statement recorded. Middleman- Whatever has been discussed here, ends here only. Inspector- Now this matter ends here. (Saying this, the inspector starts walking towards the police station. Behind him, the middleman takes out his phone from his pocket while recording a video. Then all three people go and sit in the police station.) Know the complete matter- Santosh Kumar from Karend village had applied for a gold loan at the Gahdos branch of Bank of India on February 27, 2023. His timeline was completed in August of the same year. After that, a notice came from the bank to repay the loan. The notice was not responded to. Again in December, another notice was sent. This time too, no response was received from Santosh. During the same period, Santosh's nephew Shantanu filed a missing person report at Maal police station. Now three years later in 2026, on April 14, the bank manager filed a fraud case against Santosh. SI Guddu Prasad is investigating this case registered in Special CJSM Custom. To recover that money, he goes to Santosh Kumar's house. Interrogation is ongoing for recovery. Allegation of demanding money and picking up youth from home Vishnu Kumar, brother of Santosh Kumar, has given an application to Joint CP Babul Kumar. In this, it is alleged that SI Guddu Prasad is investigating the fraud case related to his brother (Santosh). He is continuously demanding money. On May 17, 2026, his son Shantanu Dwivedi was picked up from home and taken to the police station. He was beaten up there. Later, he was released after taking ₹25,000. Reached home and misbehaved with women, demanded money It has been alleged in the petition that the SI came to the house several times. He used abusive language with the women and scared the family by banging on the door at night. The sub-inspector first pressured them to pay two lakh and later one and a half lakh rupees. He also threatened to send the entire family to jail if they didn't pay the money. The complainant has claimed to have video evidence in support of these allegations. Vishnu Kumar says that he had also filed a complaint at the Anti-Corruption Unit Control Room on May 17, 2026, but no action was taken. He alleges that this emboldened the accused inspector and the family continued to exert mental pressure. Police says further action will be taken based on investigation Rahimabad inspector Arun Trigunayak says that an impartial investigation is being conducted into the authenticity of the viral audio-video and allegations of demanding bribes. Whatever facts and evidence emerge during the investigation, departmental and legal action will be taken accordingly. The inspector was investigating the case. Recovery of 7 lakh 14 thousand rupees to be made, FIR registered In the case filed by the manager of Bank of India's Gahdos branch, it is written that Santosh Kumar had taken a gold loan of 7 lakh 14 thousand rupees. At the time of depositing the gold, according to Satyam Soni's receipt, 185 grams of gold was 23 carat. Later, when Santosh was not depositing the loan money despite notices, that gold was examined. The gold turned out to be only 19 grams and was 18 carat in total.

stories.title: Rajpal Yadav sentenced to jail in cheque bounce case:Ordered to pay ₹7.35 crore, wife fined; HC says, 'Don't treat the law like a filmy drama'
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday upheld actor Rajpal Yadav's conviction in seven cheque-bounce cases and sentenced him to three months' imprisonment in each case. Since the sentences will run concurrently, he will serve three months in jail. The court remarked, 'Don't treat the law like a film drama,' and also imposed a fine on his wife. According to Live Law, Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma directed Rajpal Yadav to pay ₹1.05 crore to the complainant in each of the seven cases. In addition, he has been asked to pay ₹1.0475 crore to the complainant and ₹25,000 to the State. The court also ordered Rajpal Yadav's wife, Radha Yadav, to pay ₹5.51 lakh as a fine to the complainant in each case. The High Court said the trial court had correctly calculated the compensation after considering the amount Rajpal Yadav had already paid as part of an earlier settlement. The court noted that Rajpal Yadav had already paid ₹2.25 crore to the complainant during the proceedings. This amount will be adjusted while calculating the remaining compensation he has to pay. The court observed that an earlier bench had given Rajpal Yadav several opportunities to settle the dispute after he expressed his willingness to resolve the matter amicably. However, despite repeated opportunities, he failed to honour the settlement and did not fulfil the promises made before the court. According to the judgment, Rajpal eventually refused to make any further payments and told the court that he was ready to go to prison instead. What is the case about? Rajpal Yadav got into this legal trouble over allegations of cheque-bounce offences. In 2010, he borrowed approximately ₹5 crore. Due to accumulating interest, penalties and payment delays, the debt increased to nearly ₹9 crore. Rajpal attempted to settle the debt with cheques that were dishonoured, leading to criminal charges under the Negotiable Instruments Act. The actor was later directed by the Delhi High Court to surrender and was sent to Tihar Jail. The court took this decision after he repeatedly missed deadlines for settlement payments set by the court and failed to honour the commitments he had made. Why did he take ₹5 crore loan? In 2010, Rajpal Yadav thought of stepping in the film direction, for which he borrowed ₹5 crore from Murali Projects Pvt Ltd. He took this amount to finance his film “Ata Pata Laapata.” However, the film did not work well at the box office and failed. This resulted in financial difficulties, and Rajpal Yadav struggled to repay the loan. Consequently, several repayment cheques bounced, resulting in a case filed under the Negotiable Instruments Act. Rajpal gets emotional after surrendering to jail Before surrendering, Rajpal Yadav expressed his financial struggles in court. According to a News X report, he said, "Sir, kya karoon? Mere paas paise nahin hain (Sir, what to do? I have no money). 'Aur koi upaay nahin dikhta… Sir, yahan hum sab akele hain (There is no other option, we all are alone here). Sonu Sood offers help Sonu Sood shared a post on X and Instagram Stories, writing: "Rajpal Yadav is a very talented actor who has given many memorable performances to our film industry. Sometimes life can be unfair, but that does not mean someone lacks talent. Time can sometimes be very harsh. He will be part of my film, and I believe this is the time for producers, directors and collaborators to stand together. The signing amount he receives, which can be adjusted against future work, is not a donation. It is a matter of his respect and dignity." Other actors also offered help to Rajpal Yadav Actor Gurmeet Choudhary has also offered support to Rajpal Yadav, urging others in the film industry to do the same. Some politicians have also come forward to offer help. Tej Pratap Yadav, president of Jan Shakti Janata Dal and son of Lalu Yadav, has offered significant financial assistance, donating ₹11 lakh to Rajpal Yadav and his family. This combined support aims to ease the challenges faced by the actor and his loved ones. According to an India TV report, after surrendering, Rajpal once again appeared before the Delhi High Court and sought relief. He told the court that he had brought a cheque for ₹25 lakh and assured the court that he would pay the remaining amount as well. He requested relief on this basis. However, the court clearly stated that surrender was necessary before any relief could be considered. The court said that only after surrender would it examine whether any relief could be granted. The High Court also clarified that the relief granted earlier was based on repeated assurances that the dispute would be resolved amicably and that the complainant company would be paid. However, the court found that, despite being given several opportunities, these assurances were not honoured. According to the court, around ₹9 crore remains outstanding. Relief withdrawn for repeatedly failing to comply with court orders Earlier, Justice Swarna Kanta Sharma said that the trial court's sentence had been stayed in June 2024 only to give Rajpal Yadav time to resolve the matter. The court noted that several deadlines had been granted, but the payments amounting to crores of rupees were not made. The court also rejected the explanation that technical or typographical errors in the demand draft had caused the delay. The court said these arguments were not credible. It further observed that the assurances had been given openly through senior lawyers and that additional time had been granted solely on the basis of the petitioner's instructions.
