stories.summary: Researchers discovered land isopods forming massive, synchronized circular formations. These creatures, known as woodlice, were drawn into glowing traps by streetlights. The isopods marched in tight circles until exhaustion or predation stopped them. This behavior, observed in Israel's Golan Heights, poses risks to the small animals. Artificial light at night can inadvertently alter natural survival strategies.

stories.title: 'Jam-packed' with cockroaches: Kunal Kamra, Chandrashekhar Azad join CJP protest on day 25
Censor Board clearance for OTT films? Govt might amend IT Rules 2021 after row over 'Satluj'
stories.summary: The government is considering mandatory Central Board of Film Certification for OTT releases. This move would require amendments to existing IT rules for digital media. A recent controversy over the film Satluj on Zee5 prompted this consideration. Action may also be initiated against Zee5 for its release while under review. State governments are responsible for enforcing laws against private screenings of uncertified films.

stories.title: The Dutch police trained eagles to catch illegal drones, but the unusual experiment was later abandoned
Bali’s 1,000-year-old rice fields once worked as a giant water system. Now 6,500 hectares have vanished and locals are buying water
stories.summary: Bali's historic subak irrigation system is under pressure from tourism expansion. Thousands of hectares of rice fields have disappeared, impacting water availability. Increased demand from tourism facilities strains groundwater resources significantly. This loss threatens the subak system and ecological balance on the island. Preserving these terraces is crucial for water security and cultural heritage.

stories.title: Singapore turned wastewater into drinking water: How Singapore has treated the sewage water into liquid gold through NEWater, achieving a sustainable supply that exceeds World Health Organisation standards
'If Ramchandra married once, Rahim too should marry once': MP CM Mohan Yadav's UCC pitch
stories.summary: Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav strongly supports implementing a Uniform Civil Code. The state government plans to introduce a UCC Bill during the upcoming monsoon session. A committee submitted its report recommending UCC implementation, excluding tribal communities. The chief minister criticized the Congress party for its stance on the UCC issue. The government will also abide by the Supreme Court's decision on the Bhojshala dispute.

stories.title: Why was Washington reflecting pool drained again weeks after $14M renovation
'I intend to kill Muslims': Indian mall worker in US stabbed by Utah man
Fijians predict when a cyclone is approaching using bees, breadfruit and ancient wisdom
Scientists cut climbing vines from a damaged Borneo forest. Its canopy then grew three times faster
stories.summary: Trimming aggressive climbing vines from logged tropical forests can substantially expedite canopy recovery, providing a more economical alternative to new tree planting for ecosystem restoration. Areas where vines were cut exhibited a carbon storage rate three times quicker than those with newly planted trees, as confirmed by laser mapping. Effective vine management promotes forestry sustainability and preserves biodiversity.

stories.title: Iran says 30 civilians killed in US strikes as Trump warns of 'hitting them harder'
For nearly 50 years, China has placed straw grids across its deserts; desertified land is now shrinking by over 1,000 sq km a year, but scientists say the fight is far from over
stories.summary: China's Green Great Wall project has fought desertification for nearly fifty years. Millions of rural laborers have used straw checkerboards and planted saplings. This effort has reduced desertified land and increased forest cover significantly. The program demonstrates a long-term political commitment to environmental restoration. Sustaining these gains requires continued local involvement and adaptation.

stories.title: Neanderthals nearly disappeared 75,000 years ago, but one small group in France repopulated Europe
'Abhishek has done no wrong': Mamata Banerjee stands firmly behind nephew amid rebellion in TMC
stories.summary: Mamata Banerjee strongly defended Abhishek Banerjee, stating he had done no wrong. She accused rebel leaders of unfairly targeting her nephew and his family. Mamata linked Madan Mitra's exit to ED summons, suggesting a 'setting' with the BJP. She asserted that a few leaders leaving would not weaken the Trinamool Congress party. The party chief vowed to rebuild the organization and continue its political fight.

stories.title: 'India needs your voice': Shashi Tharoor urges Sonam Wangchuk to end hunger strike, writes letter to Jantar Mantar protestors
stories.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor has publicly backed students protesting against examination irregularities, urging climate activist Sonam Wangchuk to stop his hunger strike. He pointed out that equitable exams are vital for young people from less privileged backgrounds. Tharoor affirms that peaceful demonstrations are necessary to amplify youth concerns, and the opposition is set to raise these student issues in Parliament next week.

stories.title: 'Kick Argentina out': Why over 10 million people signed petition against Messi's team
stories.summary: An online petition demands Argentina's expulsion from the World Cup due to alleged FIFA favouritism. Millions have signed the petition, citing perceived bias towards Lionel Messi and his team. Critics point to controversial refereeing decisions and VAR reviews in several matches. Argentina's coach dismisses these claims, calling them baseless accusations from detractors. The winners of the Argentina-England semi-final will face Spain in the championship match.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Delhi HC seeks Centre's reply on Sonam Wangchuk's PIL; Madan Mitra quits Mamata camp & more
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court requested responses regarding a PIL for climate activist Sonam Wangchuk's urgent medical intervention. Trinamool Congress MLA Madan Mitra resigned from the Mamata Banerjee faction and joined a rebel group. The Union Cabinet approved seven significant projects across various sectors, including semiconductors and railways. The United States conducted fresh military strikes targeting Iranian military sites near the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Divers have just found the first silver bar from the Spanish shipwreck in nearly 30 years
This little girl has one adorable morning routine with her three Golden Retriever pet dogs
stories.summary: A little girl begins her day with morning cuddles for her three Golden Retrievers. She hugs Riley, Twyla, and Bear individually before any other activity. The dogs remain calm and affectionate during these daily morning greetings. This routine teaches the child about love and gentle connection. The heartwarming video captures a special bond between a child and her pets.

stories.title: British man jailed in Iran on spying charges given additional two-year sentence for speaking to media, family claims
Mark Zuckerberg and Jeff Bezos cannot buy their way into this exclusive club in Florida
stories.summary: A wave of tech billionaires is transforming the real estate landscape on Miami's exclusive Indian Creek Island, snagging up luxury residences. However, simply owning a home here isn't enough to secure membership in the sought-after country club; one must be nominated and sanctioned by a board. This uptick in affluent individuals relocating to Florida from California stems primarily from concerns over impending wealth taxes in their former state.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Mike Tyson: "Fear is like fire. If you learn to control it, you let it work for you. If you don't…" - the boxing legend’s powerful lesson on controlling fear before it controls you
stories.summary: Mike Tyson viewed fear as a controllable force, much like fire. He believed controlled fear sharpens focus and aids preparation for challenges. Uncontrolled fear, however, leads to panic and poor decision-making. This perspective originated from his boxing mentor, Cus D'Amato, and shaped his career. Examining fear's signal, rather than hiding it, is key to its effective management.

stories.title: Scientists warmed the same forest soil by 5°C for 37 years; in the fourth decade, microbes began releasing carbon once thought safely locked away
stories.summary: Forest soils are releasing more carbon than previously believed. Warming temperatures cause stable soil organic matter to decompose. This decomposition releases additional carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. The process creates a stronger climate feedback loop for global warming. Updated climate models will now account for this slow carbon release.

stories.title: Switzerland built giant tunnels under the Alps to reduce truck traffic, but the project is now helping protect the country's mountains from climate threats
From Delhi to Karnataka: EC releases revised SIR schedule for electoral rolls - check new dates
stories.summary: The Election Commission has updated the schedule for electoral roll revision in six states. Draft publication dates vary, with final rolls due in October for most. Telangana's revision will see draft publication on August 10 and finalization on October 12. Haryana and Andhra Pradesh will publish draft rolls on July 31. This exercise aims to update voter lists by adding new and removing ineligible electors.

stories.title: 'Next week comes bridges, power plants': Trump says US strikes on Iran to escalate in three days
stories.summary: President Trump convened a meeting to discuss expanding military operations against Iran. The United States is currently conducting strikes targeting Iranian air defense systems. Trump warned of intensified attacks on power plants and bridges if Iran does not negotiate. Washington is also monitoring a deeply buried site believed to be part of Iran's nuclear program. Iran has continued retaliatory attacks on US military bases in the region.

stories.title: 'Combine our strengths': EU, Ukraine sign multi-billion 'drone deal' to counter Russia
2020 Delhi riots case: Court allows Umar Khalid 2 family video meetings every week
stories.summary: A Delhi court has restored activist Umar Khalid's weekly video meetings with his family. Jail authorities had previously reduced these meetings from two to one weekly session. The court found no justification for the reduction in the number of meetings. Khalid remains in jail in connection with the 2020 northeast Delhi riots conspiracy case. This order follows the rejection of his recent bail pleas by a Delhi court.

stories.title: How elephants turn footsteps into messages
stories.summary: Through the ground, elephants send and receive vibrations, a unique way of communicating that surpasses traditional airborne sounds. Their anatomy, featuring sizable middle ear components and eardrums, allows for the efficient transfer of low-frequency signals to the cochlea. Intriguingly, they can also close their ear canals at will, amplifying their ability to perceive these low frequencies. This remarkable skill unveils the depths of their sophisticated communication systems.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia is building a giant car-free region beside the Red Sea, but its futuristic city plans have changed
Big setback for Prashant Kishor, four Jan Suraaj leaders switch to BJP before Bankipur bypoll
stories.summary: Several Jan Suraaj leaders joined the Bharatiya Janata Party on Wednesday. This development occurs before the Bankipur Assembly bypoll scheduled for July 30. Prashant Kishor is contesting this election against the BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha. New entrants expressed their commitment to Prime Minister Modi's leadership and national development. The bypoll was necessitated after Nitin Nabin resigned from the assembly seat.

stories.title: A Canadian entrepreneur sold his tech company for millions, then spent $1.5 million building tiny homes for people without homes
'Protection of children is state's responsibility': Pak lawmaker seeks social media ban for under-16s
stories.summary: A Pakistani lawmaker proposed banning social media accounts for children under sixteen. This resolution aims to protect minors from online dangers and psychological distress. The proposal urges federal legislation and parental consent for account creation. Pakistan's Telecommunication Authority must enforce age verification systems. This move aligns with global efforts to regulate children's social media use.

stories.title: 120-year-old North Atlantic right whale skeleton returns to Hull Museum after 6 years
stories.summary: A nearly 120-year-old whale skeleton has returned to Hull Maritime Museum after extensive conservation work. Visitors can now crawl through a tunnel inside the rib cage, offering a new perspective. The skeleton, which is 117 years old, was originally found off the coast of New York. This critically endangered species, with fewer than 400 remaining, serves as an important historical reminder.

stories.title: 'Serious risk' to India's largest nuclear plant after sensitive files leaked on dark web: Report
Saudi Arabia warns expats of SR50,000 fine, jail and deportation for overstaying entry visas
He came to America as a slave. This Moroccan man later became one of North America's earliest explorers
Bring a python, get a pizza: A Florida restaurant is giving away free 'python pizza' if you bring a Burmese python caught in the Everglades

He lost both his arms at age two in a farm accident. Then he taught himself to, write, drive tractors, repair machinery and run a 1,300-acre farm using only his feet, building a YouTube following of more than 134,000
Calcutta HC allows Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction to hold Martyrs' Day rally, shifts venue near Birla Planetarium
stories.summary: The Calcutta high court permitted the Trinamool Congress rally on July 21. The court ordered the venue shifted from Victoria House to near Birla Planetarium. This decision aims to ensure smooth traffic flow and maintain public order. The rally attendance will be limited to 2,500 people between noon and 3:30 PM. Police will deploy adequate personnel to manage the law and order situation.

stories.title: Delhi HC seeks government's response on plea seeking medical intervention for Sonam Wangchuk
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has sought responses from the Centre and Delhi government regarding a PIL. This plea requests urgent medical intervention for climate activist Sonam Wangchuk, who is on an indefinite hunger strike. The activist-lawyer Rakesh Kumar Saini filed the public interest litigation seeking hospitalisation and supervised treatment. Wangchuk has been fasting since June 28, demanding the Education Minister's resignation over examination irregularities.

stories.title: 7 pink lakes in Australia and the science behind their unusual colours
stories.summary: Australia features numerous pink lakes scattered across diverse landscapes. These lakes display shifting colours influenced by weather and water conditions. Western Australia's Hutt Lagoon and pink and rainbow lakes are notable examples. South Australia's Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre and Lake MacDonnell also showcase vibrant hues. Victoria's Murray-Sunset National Park adds to the country's collection of these natural wonders.

stories.title: 7 Britons among 13 killed in Spain wildfire; grieving family says 'heartbroken'
A 1971 prediction by Stephen Hawking just came true with a cosmic collision 1.3 billion light-years away: Now scientists are trying to understand how
stories.summary: A cosmic collision of two black holes confirmed Stephen Hawking's fifty-year-old prediction. The observed increase in the merged black hole's area precisely matched theoretical calculations. This event provided the most accurate observational evidence for Hawking's black hole area law. Scientists collaborated across LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA to analyze the gravitational wave signal. The precise data reinforces fundamental principles of modern physics and cosmology.

stories.title: 'Abhishek Banerjee refused to step aside': Madan Mitra quits Mamata's camp, joins Ritabrata Banerjee's TMC faction
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress MLA Madan Mitra has resigned from Mamata Banerjee's faction. He joined the rebel TMC faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee on Wednesday. Mitra accused Abhishek Banerjee of refusing to step aside during the party's crisis. This development follows summons issued to Mitra's family by the Enforcement Directorate. The ED is investigating a municipal recruitment scam in West Bengal.

stories.title: New England had almost completely lost its forests by the 1800s after centuries of logging. Then nature slowly reclaimed the land in one of history's greatest forest recoveries, covering about 60% of the region once again
UK proposes overnight social media curfew for 16, 17-year-olds
Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 2,000 cases, kills 754 in fastest-growing surge
stories.summary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Ebola situation has worsened, now exceeding two thousand confirmed infections and recording 754 lives lost. This outbreak has become the most rapid on record, overwhelming health authorities. Reports of suspected cases in additional provinces suggest wider transmission, though new treatment trials targeting the Bundibugyo strain provide potential avenues for relief amid severe challenges in containment.

stories.title: 'In solidarity with Wangchuk': CJP announces 1-day mass hunger strike at Jantar Mantar tomorrow
stories.summary: The Cockroach Janata Party will hold a hunger strike on July 16 supporting Sonam Wangchuk. Wangchuk's health is declining on his eighteenth day of fasting. He has lost significant muscle mass and is experiencing immense pain. A court petition seeks to force-feed Wangchuk and move him to a hospital. This intervention is deemed necessary to preserve his life and prevent further deterioration.

stories.title: Supriya Sule rules out NDA switch, says NCP (SP) yet to decide on Delimitation Bill
stories.summary: Supriya Sule denied her party would support the Delimitation Bill without discussion. She stated the NCP (SP) remains firmly aligned with the INDIA alliance. Discussions about the bill will occur within the INDIA bloc after its introduction. Recent meetings with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis fueled merger speculation. However, NCP leaders have refuted claims of any merger talks.

stories.title: Forest City Fights Pollution:China is building a city where 40,000 trees will grow across buildings
Punjab's textile sector has immense potential, says CM Bhagwant Mann at Bharat Tex 2026
stories.summary: On Tuesday at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, Mann said Punjab is playing a significant role at Bharat Tex 2026, with 97 companies from the state participating in the exhibition.

stories.title: Andy Burnham condemns alleged right-wing terror plot at Islamic gathering, says 'hatred against Muslims has no place in UK'
'Significant moment': PM Modi as India-UK trade deal comes into effect
Swiss cows wear giant bells for a simple reason rooted in mountain life
stories.summary: In the picturesque Alps, cowbells play a crucial role for farmers overseeing their herds. These melodic bells make it easier to track cattle across expansive mountain landscapes, especially amid fluctuating weather conditions. Local traditions like Alpabzug honor this custom, showcasing beautifully adorned bells as part of cattle returning home. Interestingly, studies suggest cows become accustomed to these sounds, influencing their behavior.

stories.title: Why Taslima Nasreen's Kolkata return is a powder keg for Bengal politics
stories.summary: Taslima Nasreen's upcoming return to Kolkata after 20 years sparks intense political discussions. The Trinamool Congress and Bharatiya Janata Party both voiced their strong opinions regarding her visit. Exiled since 2007, Nasreen is set to participate in an anti-fundamentalism literary event this August. Her previous works and the circumstances of her exile have sent shockwaves through conversations about free speech and the intersection with religious beliefs in West Bengal.

stories.title: 6 most snake-filled water bodies in South Carolina: From the Savannah River to the ACE Basin
stories.summary: South Carolina's abundant waters attract many snake species, both harmless and dangerous. The Savannah River and Great Pee Dee River are home to several notable snake populations. Congaree River and Lake Murray host a variety of snakes, including venomous ones. Lake Hartwell and the ACE Basin also feature numerous water-dwelling snake species. These warm environments and plentiful prey make South Carolina ideal for snakes.

stories.title: How tiny pollen grains helped solve a brutal murder: The fascinating science behind nature's invisible crime scene evidence
stories.summary: Tiny pollen grains offer vital clues for investigators solving complex criminal cases. Forensic palynologists analyze these microscopic particles to link suspects to crime scenes. A notable murder case in New Zealand was solved using unusual mutated pollen evidence. Pollen's resistance to decomposition makes it a persistent and valuable forensic tool. This silent evidence helps identify and locate regions, aiding in criminal investigations.

stories.title: New highway hurt his town. At 98, he helped revive America's famous Route 66
In Tokyo's hidden 1,100-year-old shrine, thousands of desperate fans are praying for impossible concert tickets
Florida treasure hunters searching a 400-year-old shipwreck discovered a rare 22.5-pound silver bar worth up to $100,000

Quote of the day by Stoic philosopher Epictetus: "Any person capable of angering you becomes your master; he can anger you only when…" - why losing control of your emotions can hand power to someone else
stories.summary: Stoic philosopher Epictetus taught that anger is a choice, not an automatic reaction. He believed individuals control their responses to external provocations. This ancient wisdom remains relevant in today's digital age. Modern life offers many opportunities for emotional entanglement with others. Recognizing this power dynamic helps maintain personal control over one's day.

stories.title: Scientists fitted a European honey buzzard with a GPS tracker. The bird flew for 42 days, covering more than 10,000 km from South Africa to Finland and helping researchers uncover the secrets of one of nature's greatest migrations
China's Brahmaputra mega dam: Can it control river water flowing into India?
stories.summary: China is constructing a massive hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo River. This project raises significant water security and strategic concerns for India. Experts warn of potential impacts on downstream water flows and ecological stability. India is accelerating its own hydropower development in response to these developments. The project's long-term implications for regional water management remain under scrutiny.

stories.title: NCP reunification on cards? CM Fadnavis' talks with leaders of both factions fuels buzz
'May die in 2 days, lost 8.5 kg': Plea in Delhi HC seeks 'force-feeding' of Sonam Wangchuk as hunger strike takes toll on activist's health
stories.summary: A plea seeks court intervention to force-feed activist Sonam Wangchuk, whose hunger strike has entered its eighteenth day. Concerns are growing over his deteriorating health as he has reportedly lost significant weight. The petition urges authorities to shift him to a government hospital for medical intervention. It argues that saving his life is of paramount importance for the nation.

stories.title: Nepal court jails ex-deputy PM, home minister in fake refugee scam; 14 others convicted
stories.summary: Two former Nepal ministers received prison sentences for their involvement in a fake refugee document scam. Top Bahadur Rayamajhi was sentenced to four years, and Bal Krishna Khand received two years. Fourteen others were also convicted and sentenced for their roles in the alleged fraud. The investigation began in 2023 after authorities uncovered claims of Nepali citizens posing as refugees.

stories.title: AI wants more than your searches now
stories.summary: Internet and social media giants are looking to track how you engage with their services as they seek to improve their AI models. Here’s what you need to know

stories.title: 'Received nothing but silence': CJP's Dipke slams Centre as Sonam Wangchuk's fast enters Day 18
stories.summary: Abhijeet Dipke criticized the government's silence regarding Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike. Wangchuk has been fasting for eighteen days protesting examination irregularities and paper leaks. He questioned why the Prime Minister has not engaged in dialogue. Opposition leaders have appealed to Wangchuk to end his fast due to his health. Wangchuk has lost 8.5 kg since beginning his protest on June 28.

stories.title: Middle East war: Trump weighs 'devastating strikes'; Iran targets US bases in Middle East - key points
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard has asserted that the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until the United States changes its course of action. This comes on the heels of the US conducting new strikes near the Strait and reinstating a naval blockade. Iran has also announced attacks on US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain, exacerbating regional tensions after a recently collapsed truce.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Princess Diana: "I don't want expensive gifts; I don't want to be bought. I have everything I want. I just want someone to…" - why emotional security can matter more than wealth or luxury
stories.summary: Princess Diana emphasized that emotional security surpasses material possessions. She desired dependable presence and a feeling of safety from loved ones. This need for reassurance begins in childhood and continues throughout life. Genuine presence offers more to relationships than grand, extravagant gestures. Her words highlight the enduring human need for emotional connection and support.

stories.title: 'If she publicly says ...': Congress extends Martyrs' Day invite to Mamata, but with a condition
stories.summary: The Congress invited Mamata Banerjee to its Martyrs' Day event in Kolkata. This invitation came with a condition that she acknowledge leaving Congress was a mistake. West Bengal Congress president stated Mamata should not distort the historical significance of the 1993 movement. He added that admitting her past decision was wrong would be a significant gesture. The Congress stage remains open for her to pay respects to the martyrs.

stories.title: FBI adds Indian-origin man to most wanted list over alleged organised crime links
stories.summary: The FBI has added Nitish Kaushal to its most wanted list for his alleged role in organized crime. Kaushal is linked to the Jaggu Bhagwanpuria group involved in various illegal activities. This action follows charges against Lawrence Bishnoi and Goldy Brar for a Canadian assassination. Federal agents recently conducted large raids targeting the Lawrence Bishnoi network in the United States.

stories.title: US seismologist has been detained in China for nearly 2 years without trial: Family
stories.summary: A Chinese-born American seismologist faces spying charges in China. Youlin Chen has been detained for nearly two years, according to his wife. US officials have designated his detention as wrongful and a top priority. China denies any wrongful detention and states its judicial organs follow law. The case adds tension to the ongoing relationship between the two nuclear-armed nations.

stories.title: Where Indians come to watch, and be watched
stories.summary: From Shubman Gill and Priyanka Chopra to tennis lifers such as Lara Dutta and Ravi Shastri, Wimbledon now offers sport, style, status, and sentiment

stories.title: Cuss remarks against CJI: Two law students arrested over courtroom disruption
Boat tragedy in San Francisco: One dead, two missing after pontoon boat capsizes near Alcatraz
Thailand scraps plan to end visa-free entry for Indians
stories.summary: Thailand will now allow thirty-day visa-exempt entries for Indian visitors. This decision follows a recent drop in arrivals from India impacting tourism. The government aims to align with Indian tourist travel behavior and boost visitor numbers. Previously, Indian tourists enjoyed sixty days visa-free entry to the country. This change reverses an earlier proposal to eliminate visa-free access for many nations.

stories.title: ADAG companies siphoned off loan money via 53 shell firms: ED
stories.summary: Enforcement Directorate informed the Supreme Court about Reliance ADAG entities siphoning funds. These companies allegedly used fifty-three shell entities to divert bank loans. Assets worth over Rs 5,500 crore have been attached by the agency. Other Reliance group companies also diverted funds for luxury acquisitions. Investigations continue with significant assets attached and officials arrested.

stories.title: Supreme Court acquits man, 16 others in 26-year-old dowry case
stories.summary: The Supreme Court acquitted seventeen individuals accused in a dowry death case. This decision came after a lengthy twenty-six-year legal battle for the family. The court criticized lower courts for disregarding defense evidence without valid reasons. Substantive testimonies and credible documents presented by the defense remained uncontroverted. The apex court stressed the importance of treating all evidence equally during trials.

stories.title: Ahead of Lok Sabha session, Birla may recognise rebel TMC MPs' merger with NCPI
stories.summary: Rebel TMC MPs are set to hold their parliamentary party meeting under NCPI. They anticipate representation at the customary pre-session all-party meeting. Speaker Om Birla will decide on merger applications before the monsoon session begins. Recognition of NCPI could make it BJP's largest ally in the Lok Sabha. The rebel group is confident of approval due to their numbers.

stories.title: NCPI plans MPs meeting as Birla likely to decide on its recognition plea before session
stories.summary: Rebel TMC MPs are set to hold their parliamentary party meeting under NCPI. They anticipate representation at the customary pre-session all-party meeting. Speaker Om Birla will decide on merger applications before the monsoon session begins. Recognition of NCPI could make it BJP's largest ally in the Lok Sabha. The rebel group is confident of approval due to their numbers.

stories.title: Supreme Court fines Raina, 4 others Rs 3 lakh each for taking court for ride
stories.summary: The Supreme Court imposed a three lakh rupee cost on Samay Raina and four others. These comedians failed to hold a promised show for disabled individuals. They had previously faced court anger for mocking people with disabilities. The court accused Raina of lying and taking the judiciary for a ride. The bench warned artists against disrespecting people with disabilities and their talents.

stories.title: SOP soon to hear petitions after working hours, says Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will create a procedure for urgent petitions. This new system will address life and liberty concerns after court hours. The court agreed to explore this after a lawyer's plea for immediate access. Only cases involving life and liberty infringements will be considered. This aims to provide prompt constitutional protection to citizens.

stories.title: This man arrived at a Paris airport expecting to catch a flight. Instead, he lived there for the next 18 years
"Dumb disgusting low IQ animal": Hasan Piker's explosive Clavicular praise turns into brutal Asmongold attack
stories.summary: Hasan Piker has sparked fresh controversy after praising Clavicular for avoiding political commentary while launching a scathing attack on fellow streamer Asmongold. During a livestream, Hasan accused Asmongold of speaking on issues he does not understand and used harsh insults against him. A viral X post amplified the remarks, igniting heated debate over influencers discussing politics and their responsibility to large audiences.

stories.title: Madhya Pradesh's UCC draft proposes registration of live-in couples
stories.summary: Madhya Pradesh's draft uniform civil code requires live-in relationship registration. Couples must formally cancel registrations when relationships end, facing penalties for non-compliance. Parents will be informed of their children's live-in relationship status. Inheritance laws will change, including fathers as heirs to deceased sons' property. The proposed code will initially exclude the state's tribal population.

stories.title: "Charlie’s assassination wasn’t even about him": Candace Owens sparks outrage with explosive new Charlie Kirk assassination claim
stories.summary: Candace Owens is facing fresh backlash after making new claims about Charlie Kirk's death, suggesting he may have been killed after allegedly refusing to participate in a plot against her. A viral X post accused Owens of making the tragedy about herself and condemned her remarks. Her comments have fuelled intense online debate, with critics questioning the allegations and supporters continuing to defend her.

stories.title: India welcomes Canada's remark delinking government from Nijjar killing
Middle East crisis: Government lodges protest with Iran as sailor dies in fresh attacks
stories.summary: India summoned Iran's deputy chief of mission to protest recent attacks on commercial ships. One Indian seafarer tragically lost his life and two others were critically injured. These attacks on vessels like MT Al Bahiyah and MT Mombasa have intensified recently. India strongly condemned the violence and urged an immediate cessation of hostilities. The government seeks the restoration of free and safe navigation through international waterways.

stories.title: On South China Sea, government backs tribunal ruling against Beijing
stories.summary: India supports freedom of navigation and lawful sea uses in the South China Sea. The Ministry of External Affairs responded to a joint statement by several nations. This statement rejected China's expansive South China Sea claim as lacking legal basis. It also reaffirmed a 2016 tribunal ruling favoring the Philippines. India emphasizes peaceful dispute resolution in accordance with UNCLOS principles.

stories.title: Give Muslims alternative site for namaz: Supreme Court to Dhar administration
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will hear challenges to a Madhya Pradesh High Court ruling on the Bhojshala complex. It declined to stay the order which declared the site a temple. Muslim petitioners argued the ruling ignored historical evidence and existing arrangements. The court directed authorities to find an alternative space for Friday prayers. Structural changes to the complex are prohibited without court permission.

stories.title: Passport just a document to regulate departure of citizens from India: MEA
stories.summary: The MEA clarified passport issuance follows the Passports Act, 1967. This document regulates departure of Indian citizens from India. Official sources state a passport is not a determinant of citizenship. Less than eight percent of Indians currently hold a passport. This clarification follows recent government official remarks on the travel document.

stories.title: Air India crash: Draft final report on Ahmedabad tragedy will be ready only by October, AAIB tells Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau informed the Supreme Court about the inquiry timeline. The complex investigation into the Air India crash is expected to conclude soon. Analysis activities will be completed within six weeks, subject to external factors. A draft final report is anticipated by October 2026 for review. This timeline aligns with international practices for accident investigations.

stories.title: Vietnam boat survivor: Captain jumped, so did I
stories.summary: A survivor described the sudden Vietnam boat tragedy where the captain jumped overboard. He explained that only those who followed him into the water managed to escape. The closed boat prevented rear passengers from exiting, leading to their demise. He lost a childhood friend in the unfortunate incident. Improved island medical access could have saved additional lives.

stories.title: Need to relook if English can be considered an indigenous language: Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court questioned English's indigenous status while refusing to halt the CBSE's three-language scheme. This policy aims to promote Hindi and regional languages, aligning with constitutional goals. Petitioners argued against the scheme due to teacher and infrastructure challenges. They also noted limited availability of books on the NCERT website. The Centre and CBSE will file their responses within ten days.
